evidence.title: Educational case: basal cell carcinoma and its histologic differential
evidence.text: Basal cell carcinoma shows dermal islands of basophilic tumor cells with peripheral nuclear palisading, stromal retraction, and loose mucinous stroma. Cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma shows invasive islands of pleomorphic keratinocytes arising from the epidermis with prominent nucleoli and increased mitoses. Melanoma can show irregular nests and single pleomorphic pigmented melanocytes within the epidermis and dermis.

evidence.title: Various antibody clones of Napsin A, TTF-1, and p40 in non-small cell lung carcinoma
evidence.text: This tissue-microarray study evaluated CK5, p63, and p40 as squamous markers and Napsin A and TTF-1 as lung adenocarcinoma markers. Reported performance varied by marker and antibody clone, and combining Napsin A with TTF-1 improved sensitivity.

evidence.title: Colorectal carcinoma: pathologic aspects
evidence.text: Colorectal adenocarcinoma commonly forms malignant glands. Invasion can be accompanied by desmoplastic stroma, and glandular lumina frequently contain characteristic dirty necrosis. Benign colonic mucosa retains orderly crypt architecture and mature goblet cells without dysplasia.

evidence.title: Immunostaining for TTF-1, Napsin A, p40, and cytokeratin 5 aids differential diagnosis of NSCLC
evidence.text: The study compared marker combinations for separating lung adenocarcinoma from squamous cell carcinoma. TTF-1 and Napsin A supported adenocarcinoma, while p40 and CK5 supported squamous differentiation; the combined panel was more informative than a single stain.

evidence.title: Decision tree for pulmonary adenocarcinoma with mucinous features versus metastatic colorectal adenocarcinoma
evidence.text: A decision tree using TTF-1, SATB2, CDX2, and CK7 was developed to distinguish primary pulmonary adenocarcinoma with mucinous features from metastatic colorectal adenocarcinoma. The validation results support using multiple markers and clinical context when assigning a primary site.

Colorectal adenocarcinoma commonly forms malignant glands. Invasion can be accompanied by desmoplastic stroma, and glandular lumina frequently contain characteristic dirty necrosis. Benign colonic mucosa retains orderly crypt architecture and mature goblet cells without dysplasia.

The study compared marker combinations for separating lung adenocarcinoma from squamous cell carcinoma. TTF-1 and Napsin A supported adenocarcinoma, while p40 and CK5 supported squamous differentiation; the combined panel was more informative than a single stain.

A decision tree using TTF-1, SATB2, CDX2, and CK7 was developed to distinguish primary pulmonary adenocarcinoma with mucinous features from metastatic colorectal adenocarcinoma. The validation results support using multiple markers and clinical context when assigning a primary site.

review.assessment: The vision models are split between colon and rectal adenocarcinoma, both of which are morphologically similar; however, the de-identified report explicitly identifies the site as rectal.
rationale: The de-identified report explicitly states findings are consistent with rectal adenocarcinoma.
Morphological descriptions of irregular glandular structures and desmoplastic stroma align with colorectal adenocarcinoma characteristics [PMC:3418538-ColorectalMorphology].
MUSK and QUILTNET (baseline) correctly identified the rectal site, while CONCH and PLIP identified the closely related colon site.
discrepancies: Model inconsistency: CONCH, PLIP, and QUILTNET (prompted) classified the case as colon adenocarcinoma rather than rectal.
recommended_review: Pathologist verification of the primary anatomical site to distinguish between colon and rectal origin.
limitations: Morphological overlap between colon and rectal adenocarcinoma makes visual distinction difficult without clinical site data.
